thread:
sara: Heads up — HelioBank is seeing p99 tail latency spikes on /embeddings leading to intermittent 503s. Customer SLA at risk if we don't mitigate within ~2h. Requesting quick plan: rollback vs hotfix and clear owners.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2023-8471 — HelioBank embedding 503s (severity: p1). Paging oncall.

mike: jumping in. looking at the dedicated pool logs for helio-dedicated-1. Seeing KV cache thrash and a spike in memory allocs right before the 503s.

alisha: I can lead rollback if needed — prefer rollback to previous routing (model v3.2.1) while we triage v3.3.0. Need eng-platform to flip routing and eng-runtime to confirm no data migration required.

tom: eng-platform here. We can flip routing to fallback model, but we need a short PR that updates routing rules for customer HelioBank and a manual canary flip command. Who will own the PR and approve?

mike: I'll cut the hotfix branch and open the PR (branch: hotfix/helio-rollback). Will include a small routing-change patch and a smoke test. ETA 15m.

sara: @mike great. @tom once PR is ready, can you approve and schedule the canary flip? Also we need a rollback runbook snippet in the incident thread.

mike: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/platform/pulls/4827 — includes smoke test hitting /health and a canary flip script. cc @tom @alisha

deploy-bot: Canary deploy status: model v3.3.0 -> healthcheck failed on canary hosts 2m ago. 3/10 canaries healthy.

tom: reviewing PR now. Quick check: flipping routing will route HelioBank traffic to model v3.2.1 which is CPU-backed — expect slightly higher token latency but fewer 503s. We'll need to bump capacity for that pool for the next 2 hours. I can approve after a capacity increase ticket.

alisha: I can handle capacity bump. I'll request +2 instances to helio-pool and monitor. Doing it now.

mike: smoke test results in PR show embeddings OK on v3.2.1 locally. Attaching command used: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/embeddings -d '{"input": "test"}' | jq .`

sara: timeline proposal: 1) capacity bump (alisha) — 10m 2) tom approves PR and schedules canary flip — after capacity shows green 3) rollback/canary flip — target within 30m 4) monitor 30m then decide next steps. If any step fails, we escalate to full-lead call. Agreed?

tom: agree. Approving PR now. Leaving note to ops to watch cost impact.

alisha: capacity bump done — +2 instances added to helio-pool. Metrics showing CPU/mem stable after 3m.

mike: tagging rollout command here: `./scripts/canary-flip --customer HelioBank --to model:v3.2.1 --rollout 10%` — I'll run the flip once tom gives the go.

tom: OK to run. I'll trigger the manual routing change in 5m and coordinate with @mike for smoke verification.

sara: adding bridge roster for this incident: sara (incident lead), mike (engineer/hotfix PR), alisha (capacity/ops), tom (platform/routing). Updating runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/helio-rollback (added steps 1-5).

mike: running canary flip now. Paste output: `initiating canary flip -> routing update applied to 10% of helio traffic`

deploy-bot: Canary flip executed by mike at 18:12 UTC. Health checks rerunning.

mike: smoke tests: embeddings success on flipped canary hosts. No 503s observed in the 2m sample.

alisha: monitoring pool metrics — p99 latency dropping, error rate falling from 0.8% -> 0.02% on canary subset.

tom: promoting to 100% in 10m if metrics stay stable. I'll prepare rollback steps in case regression.

sara: Excellent. Plan B if we see regression after full promote: 1) revert routing to v3.3.0 2) open deeper runtime mem analysis ticket 3) notify customer of extended maintenance window.

mike: PR will remain open for tracking. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and suspected cause notes once we complete forensics.

sara: thanks all. For the next 60m we're on watch — ping here with any anomalies. :thumbsup:
